acceptance_criteria.criterion: DapperFilterSlotRepository.SaveAsync for a new slot (SlotId == 0) returns a FilterSlot with SlotId > 0 matching the database-assigned auto-increment value.
DapperFilterSlotRepository.SaveAsync for an existing slot (SlotId > 0) updates name and expression in the DB and returns the input entity unchanged.
DapperFilterSlotRepository.DeleteAsync removes the row; a subsequent GetAllAsync does not include the deleted slot.
SpdbConfigActiveFilterSlotRepository.GetActiveSlotIdAsync returns null when the key is absent or empty.
SpdbConfigActiveFilterSlotRepository.SetActiveSlotIdAsync(5) followed by GetActiveSlotIdAsync returns 5; SetActiveSlotIdAsync(null) followed by GetActiveSlotIdAsync returns null.
All SQL uses @Param parameterisation — no string interpolation or concatenation in queries.

summary: Implemented DapperFilterSlotRepository: GetAllAsync (SELECT with SlotId/Name/Expression column aliases), SaveAsync (INSERT + LAST_INSERT_ID() for new slots; UPDATE for existing), DeleteAsync (DELETE by slot_id). All SQL uses @Param parameterisation.

Implemented SpdbConfigActiveFilterSlotRepository: GetActiveSlotIdAsync reads 'active_filter_slot_id' key from spdb_config (returns null when absent or empty), SetActiveSlotIdAsync writes the int as string or empty string for null. Injects ISpdbConfigRepository directly (no transaction needed).
Extended IFilterSlotRepository with GetAllAsync and DeleteAsync — required by the WP acceptance criteria but absent from the WP-002 minimal spec.
Extended IActiveFilterSlotRepository with SetActiveSlotIdAsync — required by acceptance criteria, absent from WP-002 minimal spec.
Updated api-surface.md and file-tree.md in the project manifest.

comments.note: IFilterSlotRepository and IActiveFilterSlotRepository were delivered by WP-002 with only their minimum viable signatures (SaveAsync / GetActiveSlotIdAsync). WP-004 acceptance criteria required GetAllAsync, DeleteAsync, and SetActiveSlotIdAsync which were absent. These were added during WP-004 implementation. For future milestones, consider aligning the WP-002 Core interface spec with the downstream WP-004 implementation spec to avoid interface drift.

DapperFilterSlotRepository.SaveAsync uses two sequential round-trips for insert (INSERT then SELECT LAST_INSERT_ID()) because AllowMultipleStatements is not enabled on the MySqlConnectionStringBuilder in MySqlConnectionFactory. This is correct and safe (LAST_INSERT_ID() is session-scoped), but a single-statement approach (e.g. enabling multi-statement or using OUTPUT semantics) would be marginally more efficient if this becomes a hot path.

SpdbConfigActiveFilterSlotRepository injects ISpdbConfigRepository directly (unlike SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepository which injects IDbConnectionFactory as primary with an ISpdbConfigRepository test seam). The simpler injection is appropriate here (no transaction coordination needed), but the inconsistency is worth noting when onboarding new contributors to the infrastructure layer.

Discovered that migration m037 had not been applied to the spdb_tests schema — filter_slots table was absent. Fixed by adding a self-contained EnsureFilterSlotsTableExists() step in the test constructor (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS) so tests are runnable against a baseline spdb_tests schema.

comments.note: Migration m037 (filter_slots table) had not been applied to the spdb_tests schema. Integration tests self-healed via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in the constructor. DapperFilterSlotRepository.GetAllAsync uses Dapper ValueTuple projection (QueryAsync<(int SlotId, string Name, string Expression)>) and then manually maps to FilterSlot. This works correctly but is less idiomatic than using Dapper's direct POCO mapping (QueryAsync<FilterSlot>). The tuple approach was likely chosen to avoid column-name ambiguity — no action required, just worth noting for future maintainers.

No constructor null-guard test was written for DapperFilterSlotRepository because the null check throws ArgumentNullException synchronously and the constructor is straightforward. If the pattern is desired for consistency with SpdbConfigActiveFilterSlotRepositoryTests, a single [Fact] can be added in a follow-up.

summary: Reviewed 4 source files (DapperFilterSlotRepository, SpdbConfigActiveFilterSlotRepository, IFilterSlotRepository, IActiveFilterSlotRepository). 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium, 1 Low finding. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A03 (Injection) — CONFIRMED SAFE. All SQL in DapperFilterSlotRepository uses Dapper @Param parameterisation exclusively: INSERT uses @Name/@Expression, UPDATE uses @Name/@Expression/@SlotId, DELETE uses @SlotId, SELECT LAST_INSERT_ID() has no user input. SpdbConfigActiveFilterSlotRepository stores int.ToString() or string.Empty only — no injection path exists.

Low — A04 (Insecure Design) — DapperFilterSlotRepository.SaveAsync guards against a null FilterSlot record (ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull) but does not validate that slot.Name or slot.Expression are non-null before executing SQL. If either property is null and the DB column is NOT NULL, a MySqlConnector exception propagates instead of a clean ArgumentException at the method boundary. Not exploitable; recommend adding null/empty guards on Name and Expression for defensive robustness. File: src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Library/DapperFilterSlotRepository.cs, SaveAsync method.

No security findings across OWASP A01–A10 at Critical or High severity. All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed. Input validation at the DB boundary is clean. No secrets, no dynamic SQL construction, no HTTP/SSRF surface, no auth/session concerns in scope. Security sign-off granted.

summary: Code review PASS. Reviewed 4 source files and 2 test files. No blocking issues found. All acceptance criteria independently confirmed against the implementation.

DapperFilterSlotRepository: Clean, sealed, null-guarded. ValueTuple projection in GetAllAsync is correct and justified — FilterSlot's required init properties prevent direct Dapper POCO mapping. Upsert logic (SlotId==0 → INSERT+LAST_INSERT_ID; else UPDATE) is correct. All SQL fully parameterised. ConfigureAwait(false) consistent throughout.
SpdbConfigActiveFilterSlotRepository: Clean delegation pattern. null/empty and non-numeric handling via string.IsNullOrEmpty + int.TryParse is robust and graceful.
Interface contracts (IFilterSlotRepository, IActiveFilterSlotRepository) are accurate with well-written XML documentation.
Test quality is high: 17 tests across two files, comprehensive AC coverage, clean InMemoryConfigRepository stub, proper Dispose cleanup, graceful DB-skip via SkippableFact.

comments.note: DapperFilterSlotRepository.GetAllAsync uses ValueTuple projection (QueryAsync<(int SlotId, string Name, string Expression)>) with manual mapping to FilterSlot. This is correct and justified — FilterSlot uses required init-only properties, which standard Dapper POCO mapping cannot satisfy via reflection. The workaround is well-reasoned and should be preserved. Future maintainers should be aware of this constraint when modifying the FilterSlot model.

Security Auditor's Low finding re-noted: DapperFilterSlotRepository.SaveAsync guards against a null slot record but does not validate that slot.Name or slot.Expression are non-null before executing the INSERT or UPDATE. A defensive ArgumentException on null/empty Name or Expression would provide a cleaner contract boundary, but this is non-blocking.

[documentation-forward] IFilterSlotRepository.SaveAsync XML doc states 'For updates the input entity is returned unchanged' but does not document the behaviour when SlotId > 0 and no matching row exists. The current implementation executes an UPDATE that silently affects 0 rows and returns the input entity — this edge-case contract (silent no-op) should be explicitly stated in the interface docstring so callers are not surprised.
